H("B. Overruns of approved budget caps (reduced: $9,520.00)",2)
bullet(" Lines 22 and 27 together bill $40,900 for May against a $35,000 monthly cap that was approved with GC concurrence and expressly required “advance notice and Lorraine’s sign-off before the overage is incurred” (Log Entry 2). No such authorization exists. The $5,900 overage is rejected (GL §5.4 Budget Caps). Splitting May’s Hartsfield fees across two lines obscured the breach. Further, $8,400 does not correspond to whole tenths of an hour at the approved $650 rate, suggesting a rush premium not covered by the approval; any premium must be supported by Dr. Hartsfield’s original invoice and, if not approved, removed. Only the General Counsel can grant retroactive approval of this overage (GL §5.4 Monthly Threshold).","Dr. Hartsfield ($5,900).")
bullet(" Relativity hosting (Line 41) is billed at $14,200 against an approval “not to exceed $12,000” per month, which warned that charges above $12,000 without re-authorization “will be subject to reduction” (Log Entry 1). Data volume grew from the 1.8 TB estimate to 2.4 TB without notice. The predictive coding module (Line 44, $2,200) is an e-discovery processing cost under GL §5.8(a), and HWK’s own Relativity request described predictive coding as part of the approved workflow; it therefore counts against the same $12,000 cap. Total May e-discovery spend is $16,400; the $4,400 above cap is rejected (GL §5.8(b)).","E-discovery ($4,400).")
bullet(" HWK requested a $75/hour exception for R. Chen; the Relationship Attorney refused in writing on April 22, 2025 and directed that Chen be billed at no more than $65/hour (Log Entry 4). Billing 142 hours at $75 disregards that instruction. The $65 cap has no exception absent the General Counsel’s written approval, and any amount the agency charges above $65 is for HWK’s account (GL §5.9). Reduction: $1,420.","R. Chen rate ($1,420).")

H("D. Travel cap exceedances (reduced/rejected: $468.00)",2)
para("The San Francisco trip was pre-approved on the express condition that hotels stay within the $275 Tier 1 cap (Log Entry 5); HWK’s own request represented it would book within the limit. Both rooms were billed at $319/night ($176 total excess). The Washington, D.C. hotel ($348, Tier 1 cap $275) exceeds the cap by $73. Travel meals exceeded the $75 per-person, per-day cap on 5/2 ($64 excess), 5/3 for M. Beale ($7) and 5/13 for C. Aldridge ($21). The Greenville full-size rental car ($127) is a non-reimbursable vehicle class with no documented unavailability of a mid-size car (GL §5.2). No extraordinary-circumstances pre-approval was sought for any hotel overage, so the Firm absorbs the excess.")

H("E. Non-compliant working meals (rejected/reduced: $901.00)",2)
para("Non-travel meals are reimbursable only when Pinnacle personnel or third-party witnesses/parties attend (GL §5.7). Line 38 ($612 at Carmichael’s Steakhouse) and Line 39 ($24 solo desk lunch) involved Firm personnel only; Line 38 additionally included two summer associates, whose development is the Firm’s own investment (GL §3.5), and at $122.40 per head would exceed the $85 dinner cap in any event. Line 40 ($247, The Piedmont Room) was attended by HWK lawyers and plaintiff’s counsel — opposing counsel is neither Pinnacle personnel nor a witness or party — and the description omits the names and titles of the plaintiff-side attendees; we recommend rejection, while noting that this is the most judgment-dependent item in the report. If the Relationship Attorney prefers to allow it, require a compliant resubmission (attendee names/titles, itemized receipt with alcohol removed) and cap it at $85 per attendee. Line 37 (lunch with D. Yamashita) qualifies but is capped at $50 per person; $18 reduction.")
